title: Vendor Encryption & Key Management Annex - Draft
content:
Purpose and scope:

This Annex sets out the minimum encryption, key management and related operational controls that the Vendor must implement and maintain when processing Customer Data on behalf of the Customer. It supplements and forms part of the parties' Data Processing Agreement (or Master Services Agreement), and applies to all processing of Customer Data in any deployment model (hosted, dedicated, private).

1. Definitions
- 'Customer Data': data provided to Vendor by or on behalf of Customer under the applicable Agreement.
- 'Encryption at Rest': storage of Customer Data in encrypted form using industry-standard cryptographic algorithms.
- 'Encryption in Transit': use of TLS or equivalent to protect Customer Data while traversing networks.
- 'KMS': Key Management Service used to manage cryptographic keys.
- 'BYOK': Bring Your Own Key — a model where Customer provides or controls the encryption key material.
- 'HSM': Hardware Security Module used to store and operate on key material in a tamper-resistant environment.

2. Encryption Requirements
2.1 Encryption in Transit: Vendor must protect all Customer Data in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher, configured to use strong cipher suites (e.g., AEAD ciphers) and with certificate validation consistent with industry best practices. Internal service-to-service traffic carrying Customer Data must be similarly protected.

2.2 Encryption at Rest: Vendor must encrypt Customer Data at rest using AES-256 (or equivalent). Disk-level and object-store encryption must be enabled for all storage that may contain Customer Data. Logical application-layer encryption is required for particularly sensitive fields as mutually agreed.

2.3 Key Usage and Separation: Cryptographic keys used to encrypt Customer Data must be scoped and separated by Customer where feasible (tenant-scoped keys). Keys used for control-plane functions must be distinct from those that protect Customer Data.

3. Key Management and Control Models
The Vendor must support at least one of the following key control models; the selected model must be documented in the Order Form or Annex signature page.

3.1 Vendor-Managed Keys (Default): Vendor generates and manages keys within a vendor-selected KMS. Vendor must:
- Maintain key lifecycle controls (creation, rotation, revocation, archival, destruction).
- Store master keys in an HSM-backed KMS where available.
- Enforce role-based access to KMS operations and log all administrative operations.
- Rotate keys at least once every 24 months or more frequently if required by Customer policy.

3.2 Customer-Managed Keys (BYOK): Where Customer elects BYOK:
- Vendor must provide documented integration steps for Customer KMS (cloud KMS or customer-provided HSM) and limit access to Customer-controlled keys to the minimum necessary.
- Vendor must not export key material from the Customer's KMS unless explicitly authorized.
- Vendor must support automatic rekeying and key rotation as coordinated with the Customer.

3.3 Split-Key / Envelope Encryption: The Vendor may implement envelope encryption such that data keys are encrypted with a master key stored in a Customer or Vendor HSM/KMS. Key-wrapping and data-key handling must follow NIST guidelines (SP 800-57/SP 800-38F as applicable).

4. Access Control and Administrative Safeguards
4.1 Administrative Access: Access to key material (generate, decrypt, export) must be restricted based on least privilege. Access must require multi-person authorization for any production HSM administrative role (dual-control where HSM supports it).

4.2 Personnel Controls: Vendor must maintain background-screening policies for personnel with logical/physical access to key material and maintain up-to-date role inventories for key custodians.

4.3 Logging and Monitoring: All KMS and HSM administrative operations and key access events must be logged, retained for at least 12 months, and protected from tampering. Logs must be searchable and provided to Customer during an on-site or remote audit (subject to confidentiality protections).

5. Cryptographic Standards and Algorithms
Vendor agrees to use industry-accepted cryptographic algorithms and implementations. Deprecated algorithms (e.g., RC4, MD5, SHA-1 for signature generation) are prohibited. Use of FIPS 140-2/3 validated modules is required for HSMs where applicable to Customer regulatory requirements.

6. Subprocessors and Third-Party Services
6.1 Vendor will maintain an up-to-date list of subprocessors that may have access to Customer Data or key management operations. The Vendor must ensure subprocessors comply with the requirements of this Annex.

6.2 If a subprocessor is used for KMS/HSM services, Vendor must ensure contractual flow-down of the controls in sections 2–5 and provide Customer a copy of applicable certifications (e.g., SOC 2, ISO 27001) upon request.

7. Audit Rights and Evidence
7.1 Audit Access: Customer may, once per 12 months or upon reasonable cause, conduct an on-site or remote audit focused on key management controls, subject to reasonable notice and the Vendor's confidentiality obligations.

7.2 Evidence: Vendor will provide the following on request:
- Redacted copies of KMS/HSM configuration and rotation schedules.
- High-level access logs and proofs of role separation (redacted to protect other customers and Vendor confidential information).
- Copies of relevant third-party attestations (SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 certificates) covering KMS/HSM services.

8. Incident Response and Key Compromise
8.1 Notification: Vendor must notify Customer without undue delay and no later than 72 hours after discovering any suspected or confirmed compromise of key material that affects Customer Data. Notification must include scope, affected keys, remediation steps, and an initial impact assessment.

8.2 Remediation: Vendor must use commercially reasonable efforts to revoke or replace compromised keys, re-encrypt affected data as required, and provide Customer with a remediation timeline. If Customer uses BYOK and key compromise is determined to be within Customer-controlled infrastructure, Vendor will assist but is not responsible for Customer KMS misconfiguration.

9. Export Controls and Cross-Border Considerations
Vendor must comply with applicable export control laws related to cryptographic software and key material. If Customer elects to restrict keys or key storage to specific geography (e.g., within EU/EEA), Vendor will use commercially reasonable efforts to honor those constraints and document the physical location of keys.

10. Termination and Key Return/Destruction
10.1 Key Escrow and Return: Upon termination or expiration of the Agreement, Vendor will, at Customer's election, either:
- Return Customer key material and any decrypted Customer Data in a mutually agreed format; or
- Securely destroy Customer key material and all copies.

10.2 Proof of Destruction: Where destruction is elected, Vendor will provide a signed certificate of destruction for key material within 30 days of the Customer's request.

11. Transition Assistance
Vendor will provide reasonable technical assistance during key transitions (rotation, BYOK adoption or revocation, migration) and will offer a migration runbook outlining steps, estimated downtime (if any), and testing guidance. Transition work that requires significant effort may be subject to a statement-of-work and separate fees.

12. Regulatory & Certification References
Vendor represents that its KMS/HSM providers maintain standard industry certifications as applicable; Vendor will list these providers and certifications in the Order Form. Applicable frameworks include: SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, PCI DSS (where relevant), and FIPS validations for cryptographic modules.

13. Miscellaneous
- Any deviation from the controls described in this Annex must be agreed in writing by both parties.
- The Annex controls are minimum requirements and do not limit Customer's right to request enhanced controls for specific regulated workloads.

Appendix A - Practical Implementation Checklist (Vendor to attest)
- TLS 1.2+ enforced for all external and internal service traffic.
- AES-256 (or equivalent) used for data-at-rest encryption.
- KMS operations logged and retained for >= 12 months.
- HSM-backed master keys for production where available.
- Key rotation schedule established and documented.
- BYOK integration guide published and tested.
- Personnel with key access background-checked.
- Third-party KMS/HSM attestations on file.

Signature/Agreement
This Annex is a non-exhaustive set of controls intended to be incorporated by reference into the parties' Agreement. By signing the Order Form or otherwise mutually agreeing to this Annex, the parties confirm the application of its terms.
